record.Etymology: Emeneau says the form might belong in DEDR 4477; the comparison remains a ranked hypothesis.

reason: Emeneau p. 443 §6 only tentatively compares this human-hair noun with DEDR 4477. DEDR 4477 has Tamil poccu “quantity of hair” and Kannada boccu “wool, down”, but the paper contrasts the regular Brahui pōs development of DEDR 4476. Keep the installed rank-2 hypothesis; no secure direct reflex is established.

record.Etymology: Emeneau considers DEDR 1876 and 2687, preferring 2687 on the initial consonant but requiring a query for either analysis.

reason: Emeneau p. 443 §6 weighs DEDR 2687 “shrink, contract” against DEDR 1876 “recoil, shyness”. The former better fits initial k-; neither explains Brahui ž. Both are already ranked hypotheses (2 and 3), not accepted etymologies.

record.Etymology: Emeneau prefers DEDR 4135 to 4183, but the final -f- is unexplained; both are retained only as ranked hypotheses.

reason: Emeneau p. 443 §7 calls DEDR 4135 “knead, squeeze” simpler than DEDR 4183 “wring, squeeze”, but -f- remains unexplained even under the preferred analysis. Existing ranks 2 and 3 preserve both hypotheses.

record.Etymology: Emeneau suggests DEDR 2621, while leaving both an Indo-Aryan comparison and expressive reshaping open.

reason: Emeneau p. 444 §8.1 presents the DEDR 2621b “suck, sip” comparison tentatively. Expressive reshaping and a possible Indo-Aryan comparison prevent a categorical assignment; keep its rank-2 hypothesis.

record.Etymology: Emeneau splits this homonymous sense from 'be slaughtered' and leaves it without etymology.

reason: The source separates this “turn sour (milk)” sense from homographic taṛifing “be slaughtered”, which is securely assigned to DEDR 3029. Emeneau p. 444 §11 explicitly leaves the sour-milk sense unetymologized.

record.Etymology: Emeneau finds no secure Dravidian, Indo-Aryan, or Iranian etymology; CDIAL 5228 remains only a tempting possibility.

reason: Emeneau p. 446 §15 n. 6 finds CDIAL 5228 tempting for “tongue” but leaves the reconstruction and immediate borrowing source unresolved. The rank-2 CDIAL hypothesis is retained; the source variant duvī has an existing rank-1 lexical link to dūī, not a resolved etymon.
